DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.769/2009 dated 05.06.2012 by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Puttur, D.K., by NC:
2023:KHC:24943 which the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the deceased died due to heart attack and not due to accidental injuries.
2.

The brief facts of the case are that on 28.12.2008, at about 4.00 p.m., the deceased being a pedestrian was proceeding near Sampya Maszid of Aryapu village by the side of the road, at that Sri. Keshava Gowda vs Mr. M Hydar on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182236799/
2 time a Cheverolet Tavera Car bearing Reg.No.KA-19-Z-8526 came from Sullia side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to her.

sentences.text: Due to which, she sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries sustained.
Therefore, the claimants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.

In the present case, the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the deceased died due to heart attack and not due to accidental injuries based upon PM report and without considering other NC: 2023:KHC:24943 evidence on record such as nature of injuries sustained by the deceased.
The accident was caused on 28.12.2008.
The deceased was taking treatment as inpatient till 24.01.2009 and was discharged from hospital and it was advised by the doctors that chances of survival of the deceased was bleak.
Therefore, deceased was discharged from the hospital and on 08.02.2009 the deceased died i.e., within a span of less than two months from the date of accident.
Till the date of death, the deceased was under continuous medical treatment.
The factum of accident, involvement of the vehicles and injuries sustained by the deceased are not disputed.

As per medical evidence on record including evidence of doctors PWs-2 and 3, it is proved that deceased has suffered following injuries:-
"1. Patient is in dazed condition,
2. A lacerated wound over the head-bleeding.
3. A lacerated wound on the nose proximal aspect-bleeding.
4. A lacerated wound on the upper lip- bleeding.
NC: 2023:KHC:24943 5. Lacerated wound on (R) forearm-bleeding (the result of the x-ray found that there was a # of radius)
6.
Multiple abrasion on the (R) brain.

7. Axonal injury of the brain."
5. Ex.P.24 is CT scan report and Ex.P.23 is Lab report, which show that deceased had sustained grievous injuries to the brain.

Brain and skull of human beings are vital organs and an injury caused to brain certainly affects other organs of the body such as lungs, heart, kidney, liver etc., because the brain nerve controls all the organs to the human body.
Injury to brain certainly accelerates the impact of adversity on other organs of body including heart and lungs.
6. In the PM report of the deceased, the cause of death is shown as 'death is due to acute myocardial infarction'.
As the deceased was aged about 71 years at the time of accident, she might have suffered Sri. Keshava Gowda vs Mr. M Hydar on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182236799/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 heart attack.
The heart attack accelerates from the brain functions.
When some part of brain is injured, if there is any injured NC: 2023:KHC:24943 nerve connected to the heart, then there are chances of acceleration of causing heart attack.
Just because in the PM report it is stated that 'death is due to acute myocardial infarction', that does not mean that heart attack has caused naturally to a living person.
But in the present case, the deceased had sustained injury to the brain also as it is evident from the PM report while examining the skull part of the body.
Therefore, considering the chronological events of date of accident and date of death, certainly the death is result of the accidental injuries as discussed above.
In this regard, the Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence on record correctly resulting into erroneously dismissing the claim petition.
7. It is the duty of the police to mention in the Unnatural Death Report (UDR) regarding consideration and analyzation of what is genesis of causing heart attack.

In the background of the facts, circumstances and evidence involved in the case as above discussed, NC: 2023:KHC:24943 considering the chronological date of events i.e., date of accident, date of discharge from the hospital and the period undergone in the hospital for treatment, it is proved that there is a nexus between the injuries sustained and death occurred.
Therefore, certainly it is proved that the deceased died due to accidental injuries.
In this regard, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside and accordingly, it is set aside.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for compensation on account of death of the deceased in the accident.
8. In the present case, the deceased was doing Coolie work and was also doing household work.
The accident is of the year 2008.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is Rs.4,500/- p.m. as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the deceased was 71 years old, therefore, the appropriate multiplier is '5'.
As the claimants are a major son and two daughters, 50% of the income is to be deducted towards her personal expenses.

Therefore, the NC:
2023:KHC:24943 loss of dependency is hereby re-assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.4,500 x 50% x 5 x 12 = Rs.1,35,000/- Accordingly, a sum of Rs.1,35,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency'.

9. The claimants are son and two daughters and therefore, they are entitled Rs.1,20,000/-
(40,000/- each) under the head 'loss of consortium'.
10.
The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'funeral expenses and transportation charges'.
11. The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'Loss of estate'.
12. From the evidence on record, it is proved that claimants have spent a sum of Rs.27,000/- in total towards medical expenses and hospitalization charges.
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.27,000/- is awarded NC: 2023:KHC:24943 under the head 'Medical Expenses and hospitalization charges'.

13. Thus, in all, the claimants are entitled for the following sums:

1. Funeral expenses and 15,000.00 transportation charges 2.
Loss of consortium 1,20,000.00 3. Medical expenses and 27,000.00 hospitalization charges 4. Loss of dependency 1,35,000.00 5. Loss of estate 15,000.00
The appellants/claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,12,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

13. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed.

The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.769/2009 is hereby set aside and the claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.3,12,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

iii. 
The claimants are not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 59 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Ordered accordingly.
